name: Beran the Supply Master

facts.text: Level 78, 30,000 health. Every 15-35 seconds he ignites a barrel that explodes (an 'Explosion' add, level 80).
He yells for help to ogres called 'onstal hyrde'. On-stael means 'arrangement, disposition' (Bosworth-Toller); 'keepers of the stores' is our reading.

story:
Every hall needs someone to count the casks, and Krondon's ogres gave the job to Beran. He took the hall's old title of keeper of the stores and kept the stores the way an ogre would: he found the pitch and the lamp-oil the old keepers had laid by for siege and winter, and he learned what happens when a torch meets a cask. Now his storerooms are stacked to the roof with barrels he can set alight whenever he likes, and his under-keepers come running when he bellows. He is not the strongest lord of Krondon, but he is the one most likely to bring the ceiling down on you.

The keeper of the stores. Every hall needs someone to count the casks, and when Orylle handed out the titles she gave Beran the old keeper's: the hyrde of the stores. The hall-folk had laid by pitch and lamp-oil for siege and winter in stacks to the roof, and Beran, who had never seen a cask in his life, opened one, put a torch to it to see what was inside, and lost his eyebrows. He has been in love with the stores ever since.

His under-keepers. He keeps them as an ogre would: he lights a cask whenever strangers come, every half minute or so, and watches it go up with great satisfaction, and bellows for his under-keepers, the onstal hyrde, who come running. The old word onstal meant arrangement, the setting of things in order. Beran arranges things in the sense that a falling ceiling arranges a room. The other lords of Krondon keep their distance from his stores, and Deben the Rightful, who needs the pitch for his muster, has never once won an argument with him.
legend:
Watch the barrels. Every half minute or so he lights one, and you do not want to be next to it when it goes. Kill his store-keepers when he shouts for them, then finish him. Raids that stood in one heap around him went home in one heap.

When he yells for help, his under-keepers come: kill them before they get to the casters. Spread out the whole fight; the barrels go off where they stand, and a packed raid loses a group to every cask. The old hands say the casks always go up where the raid is thickest, which is only another way of saying: do not be thick. Kill Beran near the doorway, not in the middle of the stacks.

loremasterTopic.text: The ogres' keeper of the stores. He found the old siege pitch of Krondon and learned what a torch does to a cask. Spread out when you fight him, and kill his keepers when he calls.

bookPage: Beran, the ogres say, had never seen a cask until he came to Krondon. He opened the first one in the stores, put a torch to it to see what was inside, and lost his eyebrows, and from that day he has loved the stores as a miser loves his gold. When we came he lit a cask and bellowed for his keepers in the same breath, and stood in the smoke laughing. We spread out across the stores like men crossing a frozen lake. When he fell, the ogres who keep the casks under him simply sat down among the barrels and waited for a new master.
